transcript: In 1929, the American astronomer Edwin Hubble discovered that the more distant a galaxy was, the faster it was moving away from us. This showed that the entire universe was expanding. If the universe is expanding now, then in the past everything must have been small, hot and gathered into a single point. From this idea, the theory of the Big Bang was born. Today, the universe is believed to have begun about 13-8 billion years ago. In the Big Bang In its first few minutes, hydrogen and helium were created And over hundreds of millions of years, the first stars ignited In 1965, the American researchers, Penzias and Wilson detected weak microwave radiation coming evenly from every direction of the sky This is called the Cosmic Microwave Background and it is regarded as the afterglow of the Big Bang It became decisive evidence for the Big Bang theory Our Milky Way galaxy is set to hold between 200 and 400 billion stars In the universe, there are said to be roughly, roughly the same number of galaxies But 95% of the universe still remains a mystery to us dark matter Which we cannot directly observe and dark energy Which is accelerating the expansion of the universe To uncover the nature of these is the greatest challenge of modern physics The James Webb Space Telescope, launched in 2021, is now bringing to us The light of the earliest galaxies of the universe Light born 13, 8 billion years ago is finally reaching the Earth You

segments.text: In 1929, the American astronomer Edwin Hubble discovered that the more distant a galaxy was,
the faster it was moving away from us.
This showed that the entire universe was expanding.
If the universe is expanding now, then in the past everything must have been small, hot and gathered into a single point.
From this idea, the theory of the Big Bang was born.
Today, the universe is believed to have begun about 13-8 billion years ago.
In the Big Bang
In its first few minutes, hydrogen and helium were created
And over hundreds of millions of years, the first stars ignited
In 1965, the American researchers, Penzias and Wilson
detected weak microwave radiation coming evenly
from every direction of the sky
This is called the Cosmic Microwave Background
and it is regarded as the afterglow of the Big Bang
It became decisive evidence for the Big Bang theory
Our Milky Way galaxy is set to hold between 200 and 400 billion stars
In the universe, there are said to be roughly, roughly the same number of galaxies
But 95% of the universe still remains a mystery to us dark matter
Which we cannot directly observe and dark energy
Which is accelerating the expansion of the universe
To uncover the nature of these is the greatest challenge of modern physics
The James Webb Space Telescope, launched in 2021, is now bringing to us
The light of the earliest galaxies of the universe
Light born 13, 8 billion years ago is finally reaching the Earth
